name: Atorvastatin
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: Start 10 or 20 mg once daily (40 mg if LDL-C reduction >45% is needed); range 10 to 80 mg once daily

key_interactions.effect: Higher atorvastatin levels or additive myopathy risk.

key_interactions.action: Do not exceed atorvastatin 20 mg; monitor for myopathy.

key_interactions.drug_or_class: HIV and HCV protease inhibitors (e.g., tipranavir/ritonavir, glecaprevir/pibrentasvir)
key_interactions.action: Tipranavir/ritonavir and glecaprevir/pibrentasvir: not recommended. Others: dose caps of 20 or 40 mg per the label.
Give at the same time as atorvastatin.

serious: Rises in HbA1c and fasting glucose
Hemorrhagic stroke risk with 80 mg after recent stroke or TIA

contraindications: Acute liver failure or decompensated cirrhosis
Hypersensitivity to atorvastatin or any excipient
monitoring: LDL-C as early as 4 weeks after starting or changing the dose
Muscle symptoms, especially when starting, titrating or adding an interacting drug

pk.bioavailability: About 14% (parent); about 30% HMG-CoA reductase inhibitory activity
pk.metabolism: Extensive, CYP3A4; substrate of OATP1B1/1B3, P-gp and BCRP
pk.active_metabolites: Ortho- and parahydroxylated metabolites (about 70% of circulating inhibitory activity)
pk.excretion_renal_pct: Less than 2% in urine; mainly biliary
pk.dialyzability: Not expected to be significantly removed (highly protein bound; label).
